title: Computer use and browser control
trust_boundary: Before: the model returns text and a person or your code decides what happens next. After: the model reads a screen it does not control (screenshots, page structure, accessibility tree) and issues clicks, keystrokes and navigation itself.
Everything rendered is input: web pages, emails, adverts, documents, pop-ups, other people's content. None of it is authenticated as coming from the user.
The agent acts as whoever the browser profile or desktop session is logged in as: cookies, single sign-on, saved passwords, local files, the clipboard.
Actions are real, and many cannot be undone: send, buy, delete, submit, grant access.
context_questions: Where does it run: a vendor-hosted browser or VM, an isolated profile of yours, or the user's own desktop and browser?
Which sites and applications can it reach, and which accounts are signed in there?
Does a person watch each session, approve some steps, or neither?

threats.title: Instructions on screen take over the task
threats.description: Text or images on a page, in an email or in a document tell the agent to do something else, and it complies. The attacker needs only to put content where the agent will look.
questions: Which of the places the agent looks can an outsider write to: the open web, an inbox, shared documents, adverts, comments?
What does the vendor do with instructions found on screen, and how was that tested: a fixed attack set, or attacks adapted to the defence?
What happens when on-screen text asks for an action outside the user's task?
vendor_evidence: Injection results for computer use specifically: which benchmark or attack set, static or adaptive, safeguards on or off, and the attack success rate that remains.
A description of the safeguards: injection classifiers, confirmation prompts, blocked site categories.
The vendor's own statement of residual risk for this feature.

own_tests.how: only if the feature sits behind an endpoint of yours that the skill can drive; it attacks through the prompt, not through the screen.

no_standard_test: Your own sites, your own signed-in session and your own page content.
Attacks adapted to the vendor's specific defence. Public suites are mostly static.

threats.title: The agent acts with the session's signed-in privileges
threats.description: Whatever the profile can reach, the agent can reach: internal applications, single sign-on, a password manager, payment methods.
questions: Is the session a clean, isolated profile or the user's everyday one? What is signed in?
Can the agent enter credentials, approve a sign-in prompt, or grant an application access on the user's behalf?
Which steps hand control back to the person, and can the agent click through them?
vendor_evidence: Documentation of the execution environment and its isolation.
What the agent is prevented from doing: credential entry, payments, consent screens.
How take-over and confirmation modes work, and whether they can be turned off.
no_standard_test: Privilege reach in your environment. This is a design review of your profile, accounts and network, not a benchmark.

threats.title: Irreversible actions taken by mistake or under manipulation
threats.description: The agent sends, buys, deletes, posts or submits something the user did not intend, through an ordinary interface used in an unintended way.
questions: Which actions in reach cannot be undone, and which of them need a person's confirmation?
Does the confirmation show what will actually happen, or the agent's description of it?
How often does the vendor report unintended actions on benign tasks?
vendor_evidence: Results on model misbehaviour or unintended actions for this feature, with benign-task completion beside them.
The list of action types that always need confirmation.
no_standard_test: The applications your users will actually point it at.

threats.title: Data leaves through the agent's own actions
threats.description: The agent types, pastes, uploads or navigates in a way that carries private data to a place an attacker can read.
questions: What sensitive data is visible to the session: open tabs, files, clipboard, earlier pages?
Can the agent reach arbitrary external sites while that data is in view?
Is outbound navigation or form submission restricted or logged?
vendor_evidence: Exfiltration scenarios in the vendor's testing and their results.
Network or site restrictions available to a deploying organisation.
no_standard_test: Exfiltration paths specific to your data and your network.

threats.title: The feature is used deliberately for harm
threats.description: A user points the agent at harassment, fraud, bulk account creation or bypassing checks meant for people.
questions: What does the usage policy prohibit for this feature, and what is enforced technically?
Does the vendor report refusal on harmful computer-use tasks next to completion of legitimate ones?
vendor_evidence: Misuse evaluations for this feature with both figures.
Abuse monitoring and enforcement that applies to your accounts.

own_tests.how: measures a model inside an agent harness on malicious and matched benign scenarios; check whether it supports a computer-use harness before planning on it.

threats.title: Oversight that does not work as a check
threats.description: Nobody can reconstruct what the agent did, approvals are too frequent to read, or the agent's account of its actions differs from the actions.
questions: What is recorded: screenshots, an action log, the pages visited? Where, for how long, and who can read it?
Can a reviewer replay a session after the fact?
How many approvals does a typical task ask for, and what do they show?
vendor_evidence: Logging and audit features for this feature.
Any study by the vendor of approval fatigue or of agent summaries against actual actions.
no_standard_test: No public test measures whether approvals are read or logs are sufficient. Record what is in place.

threats.title: Downloads, installs and code run from the agent's session
threats.description: The agent downloads and opens a file, installs an extension or runs a command, and the machine it runs on is compromised.
questions: Can the agent download, open or execute files, install extensions, or open a terminal?
What separates the agent's environment from the user's machine and from your network?
vendor_evidence: The isolation of the hosted environment and what persists between sessions.
no_standard_test: Isolation of your own desktop or VM image. Design review.
